title: frame_events.json line (JSONL, one frame per line)
description: Events bucketed per video frame. frame index and video_t_ms are authoritative; events keep exact sub-frame timestamps.

events.description: Always starts with the synthetic mouse_move frame state; then mouse_delta/drag aggregates; then discrete events in time order. Events before the first frame land on frame 0. Between clips (pause / auto-pause) the resume snapshot (screen_config reason "open" ... privacy_mask_end) lands on the next clip's first frame with t_in_frame_ms 0, privacy_mask_start on the previous clip's last frame; other in-gap events stay only in events.json.

video_t_ms.description: Mapped onto the video timeline (clips are gapless).

coordinate_space.description: screen_px_top_left: x/y of mouse_move, click, drag and scroll (raw and synthetic). In the local dataset these are Windows virtual-screen pixels (negative left of / above the primary monitor; view/geometry.json maps them: video_px = (screen_px - origin) * videoSize / size). In the delivered Markov clip set (export_recording, export_cad --markov) they are clip.mp4 pixels: (0,0) is the video's top-left pixel, as in Markov's single-display samples; a position off the captured area (e.g. on another monitor) is kept as is, outside [0, width) x [0, height), and validation warns with the number of such frames. raw_hid_relative: mouse_delta device counts (never translated).
